root_cause.text: In `fs/smb/client/smb2inode.c::smb2_unlink()`, the request I/O vectors (`open_iov` and `close_iov`) were used in `rqst` before being zero-initialized, so if `SMB2_open_init()` or `SMB2_close_init()` failed the subsequent cleanup/`smb2_set_related()` path operated on uninitialized `rq_iov` data and could oops.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE states that on `SMB2_open_init()` or `SMB2_close_init()` failure “the iovs set @rqst will be left uninitialised, hence calling SMB2_open_free(), SMB2_close_free() or smb2_set_related() on them will oops,” and the patch fixes this by adding `memset(open_iov, 0, sizeof(open_iov));` and `memset(&close_iov, 0, sizeof(close_iov));` before assigning them to `rqst`, plus moving `smb2_set_related(&rqst[1]);` after checking `rc`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize `open_iov` before use in `smb2_unlink()` to avoid using stale request I/O vector data.
intent_record.what: A new `memset(open_iov, 0, sizeof(open_iov));` call was inserted before assigning `open_iov` to `rqst[0].rq_iov` and setting `rqst[0].rq_nvec` in `smb2_unlink()`.
intent_record.how: This ensures the `open_iov` array is initialized to all zeros before it is used to build the request, preventing stale or uninitialized I/O vector contents from being sent or interpreted at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix smb2_unlink() by properly initializing the close request and setting compound related state only after successful close request setup.
intent_record.what: In smb2_unlink(), the code now zero-initializes close_iov with memset() before assigning it to rqst[1].rq_iov/rq_nvec, and it moves the call to smb2_set_related(&rqst[1]) to after SMB2_close_init() succeeds instead of calling it unconditionally before the return check.
intent_record.how: This ensures the close request iovec starts in a clean state and that the compound-related flag is only applied when SMB2_close_init() has successfully populated the request; if initialization fails, the request is now left unmodified and the error path is taken immediately.
